content.text: Direct Acting – mimic NE/EPI by directly binding to adrenoreceptor
: short-acting beta-2 agonist; binding @ beta-2 receptors → relaxation of bronchial smooth muscles & bronchodilation
: nervousness, tremor, tachy, palpitations, cough, hyperglycemia, hypokalemia
MOA: Compete w Cl in Na/K/2Cl cotransport ->⍉ reabsorb
↓ preload (↓ vol) & ↓ afterload (NO -dilator) b/c most Na reabsorb
Clin Use: ↑efficacy diuretic & remove Na/Cl from body->↑↑↑ urine
Administration: can be based on pt daily wt
Ototoxicity:↑w aminoglycoside, ↑dose, rapid IV admin, ethacrynic acid
Acute hypovolemia: rapid ↓ vol -> hypotension, shock, arrhythmia
Also AE: dizziness, rash, ↑cholesterol, anorexia, urinary bladder spasm, blurred vision
Efficacy- improve S/Sx edema and/or BP
•block sodium/Cl reabsorb in the thick ascending loop of Henle by interfering w/ the chloride-binding co-transport system
•increases excretion of Na, K, Cl, Mg, Ca, & H2O
: ⍉mortality benefit in HF pts; used to relieve sxs related to congestion/edema
: ↓ Na, K, Cl, Mg, Ca, hyperuricemia, ↑BG, ↑TG/total cholest, orthostatic hypotension, photosensitivity, ↑urination
-    Torsades de pointes: IV magnesium sulfate in dextrose to replenish Mg; K + Ca replacement may be needed
-    MC lyte cause of torsades = hypoMg (often 2/2 loop diuretics + GI losses); stable → IV magnesium + close monitoring
-    Hyperkalemia: membrane stabilization — calcium gluconate or chloride (immediate, lasts 20–30 min)
